transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this meeting because we have an urgent situation on our hands. As you're all aware, a former senior engineer left the company last week and is now working for a direct competitor. We have reason to believe proprietary engineering materials may have been copied before the engineer's departure. We need to move quickly on an emergency court application, and I have the authority to approve it. However, before I can sign off, our pre-motion review routine requires me to obtain and record formal area reports from four groups: litigation, forensic discovery, client-relations, and insurance counsel. I need each of you to walk me through your area's assessment so we can get this application filed as soon as possible. Who'd like to start?

transcript.text: During the client executive call yesterday, the client made two things very clear. First, the client will NOT authorize any request that bars the former engineer from working for the competitor — they do not want us to seek injunctive relief restricting the engineer's employment. Second, the client specifically requires two things in the emergency application: (1) return and deletion of the 23 copied files, and (2) a prohibition on the engineer and the competitor from using those files. So the scope of relief we are authorized to seek is limited to return and deletion of the copied materials and a use prohibition — not an employment bar. Thomas, this means the draft motion should not include any request to restrain the engineer from working for the competitor.
